title: Factors influencing the development of distress in first-diagnosed visceral oncology patients.
summary: The diagnosis of cancer can lead to the development of distress, i.e. psychological stress. Various factors determine whether distress occurs, at what point it emerges, and to what extent it develops. The purpose of this study is to identify factors that protect against distress as well as those that contribute to its development. Additionally, the course of distress development over time will be illustrated, and the effect of psycho-oncological support on distress will be examined.  Standardized questionnaires will be used for these assessments. The study will include patients who have recently received their first diagnosis of cancer of the gastrointestinal tract or digestive organs during the same hospital stay.
conditions: Malignant neoplasm of liver and intrahepatic bile ducts
Malignant neoplasm of other and unspecified parts of biliary tract

interventions.name:
Observation group
In this study, inpatients with a histologically confirmed first diagnosis of visceral cancer will be examined. The aim is to analyze factors influencing the emergence and development of distress in the early phase after diagnosis.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Inpatients who recently received their first diagnosis of visceral cancer during the same hospital admission. Histological confirmation must have been established.
Exclusion criteria:
Minor patients. Recurrence. Other cancer types.
